```{r scaffold-guard, include = FALSE}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# REMOVE THIS CHUNK once step 6 below is done.
#
# paper.Rmd renders to paper.md. Right now it holds instructions rather than the
# paper, so rendering it would overwrite paper.md with these notes and lose the
# article. This stops that from happening by accident.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
stop(
  "paper.Rmd is still a scaffold. Rendering it now would overwrite paper.md ",
  "with the migration instructions. Follow the steps in paper.Rmd, then delete ",

)
```

# How to turn paper.md into a rendered document

`paper.md` is hand-written today, which is why its Table 1 drifted out of step with
the code. This file is the scaffold for making `paper.md` a generated artifact, the
way `README.md` already is. Nothing has been migrated yet.

Work through the steps below. Each one is independent, so they can land in separate
commits.

## 1. Bring the YAML front matter across

Copy the whole block between the opening and closing `---` at the top of `paper.md`
into the top of this file, **below** the `output:` block that is already here. JOSS
reads `title`, `authors`, `affiliations`, `tags`, `date` and `bibliography` from it,
so it has to survive into the rendered `paper.md` — which is what
`preserve_yaml: true` above is for. Do not drop the PDL editors line underneath the
author list.

## 2. Bring the body prose across

Copy everything after the closing `---` of `paper.md`. Leave the tables and figures
alone for now; steps 3 and 4 replace them.

## 3. Replace the two tables with chunks

Delete the hand-written markdown tables and their captions, and put these in their
place. `make tables` regenerates the source files from real pipeline output, and the
`paper` target in the Makefile runs it first. Paths here are relative to this file,
which lives in `analysis/`.

````
```{r table1, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat(readLines("tables/table1.md"), sep = "\n")
```
````

````
```{r table2, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat(readLines("tables/table2.md"), sep = "\n")
```
````

Note that the generated Table 1 has **nine** rows, not the ten in `paper.md` today.
The published version listed `bout_start`, `median_speed` and `duration`, which
`summarize_walk_bouts()` returns rather than the epoch-level dataset, and omitted
`time` and `speed`, which the epoch-level dataset does have. The article text may
need a matching correction.

## 4. Replace the figures with chunks

The three figures are one function call each. Replace the `![...](fig2.png)` embeds
with chunks along these lines, keeping the existing captions:

````
```{r fig1, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "..."}
generate_activity_bout_plot(make_activity_bout_example(), bout_number = 1)
```
````

The second and third need the matched example data:

````
```{r setup-figures, include = FALSE}
source("../load.R")
example_data <- make_dwell_and_walk_example()
```
````

Then `generate_dwell_vs_walk_plot(example_data$accelerometry_counts,
example_data$gps_data)` for Figure 2 and
`generate_bout_plot(example_data$accelerometry_counts, example_data$gps_data,
bout_number = 2)` for Figure 3.

These will not match the committed PNGs. Figure 2 was drawn by hand and has no
source anywhere; Figure 3's plotting code was never committed. Compare old against
new before deleting `fig2.png`, `fig_3.png` and `fig_5.png`, and expect the article
to need updating rather than the other way round.

## 5. Fix the citations

`paper.md` contains **zero** `@` characters, so not one of its nine citations
resolves. They are written as inline code spans — `` `[Kang:2013]` `` — which render
as literal monospace text and produce no bibliography. Each needs two fixes: drop the
backticks, and convert the colon to a hyphen with an `@`, giving `[@Kang-2013]`.

The keys in `refs.bib` all use hyphens. Three are never cited: `Steel-2021`,
`Kang-2018` and `Huang-2017` — cite them or remove them.

There is also an unresolved review comment still in the source, around the Figure 1
discussion, beginning `<!-- JLG:`.

## 6. Delete the scaffold-guard chunk

The `stop()` at the top of this file exists only to protect `paper.md` while this
scaffold is unfinished. Once steps 1 to 5 are done, delete that chunk.

## 7. Render

```
make paper
```

That runs `make tables` first, then renders this file to `paper.md`. Check the result
before committing: `preserve_yaml` is easy to get wrong, and JOSS will not build
without the front matter.

To confirm the citations resolve, which `make paper` does not check:

```
cd analysis && pandoc --citeproc --bibliography=refs.bib paper.md -o /tmp/paper.pdf
```
